tasks.title: Fix the stored shape: folder layout, file names, document id, options hash, config roots
acceptance: `tests/test_docling_store.py::test_doc_id_is_slug_and_12_hex` passes: `doc_id_for(url, pdf_bytes)` gives `<last URL part, at most 40 characters>_<first 12 hex of sha256(bytes)>`, with `doc` as the fallback slug
`::test_options_hash_is_stable` passes: the same options dict in another key order gives the same 8-character hash; a changed option gives another
`::test_folder_path` passes: `<root>/<doc-id>/docling@<hash8>/` with `doc.raw.json`, `doc.json`, `run.json`

`config.PARSED_ROOT` defaults to `~/Nextcloud/Datasets/ema_nlp/parsed` (override `EMA_PARSED_ROOT`); `config.DOCLING_ENV` defaults to `~/.local/share/ema_nlp/envs/docling` (override `EMA_DOCLING_ENV`)
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: The module is pure Python and runs in .venv: no Docling import. Proposal section 'What is stored'. A 6-character hash, as doctool uses (ids.py:124-131), gave an expected 4% chance of a silent overwrite; 12 characters are used. Two PDFs with the same bytes share one folder. The parsed root is open question 1 of the proposal (the owner decides after batch 0); batch 0 writes plain JSON under the default root and reports the gzip size beside it.
tasks.outcome: corpus/parsers/docling_store.py (pure Python): slug_for, doc_id_for (<slug, at most 40>_<12 hex of sha256(bytes)>), options_hash (8 hex of canonical JSON), parse_folder (<root>/<doc-id>/docling@<hash8>/), parser_version (<docling version>+<hash8>), file names doc.raw.json, doc.json, run.json, failures.jsonl. config.PARSED_ROOT (default ~/Nextcloud/Datasets/ema_nlp/parsed, EMA_PARSED_ROOT) and config.DOCLING_ENV (default ~/.local/share/ema_nlp/envs/docling, EMA_DOCLING_ENV). 6 tests in tests/test_docling_store.py. Callers follow in TASK-009 and TASK-011. Gates: make test 792 passed, 2 skipped, 13 deselected; make lint All checks passed.

tasks.title: Build the parse environment with pinned versions, outside .venv, and prefetch its models
acceptance: `make parse-env` builds a Python 3.12 environment at `config.DOCLING_ENV` from `requirements/parse-docling.txt` (docling 2.153.0, docling-core 2.108.0, docling-ibm-models 4.0.5, docling-parse 7.28.0, rapidocr 3.10.0, transformers 5.24.1, torch 2.15.0, onnxruntime 1.32.0, pypdfium2 5.15.2, pymongo, python-dotenv) and installs this repository into it with `--no-deps`

The script downloads `en_PP-OCRv5_rec_mobile`, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 at revision `c5630abae1d940eafe0697512a0325494b02ab42` and Heron at `8f39ad3c0b4c58e9c2d2c84a38465abf757272d8`, and prints each file's SHA-256
After `make parse-env`, `.venv/bin/python -c 'import torch; print(torch.__version__)'` still prints 2.10.0 and `import docling` fails in .venv
pyproject registers the marker `gpu`; `make test-parse` runs the tests marked `parse` in the parse environment; `make test` deselects them
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Exploration section 7: installing Docling into .venv would move torch 2.10.0 under the embedding model to 2.15.0. The trial environments of the exploration (~/.local/share/ema_nlp/envs/docling-a, docling-b) proved the install; `make parse-env` makes it reproducible. The English recognition model is not in the rapidocr wheel; RapidOCR fetches it from modelscope.cn on first use, so the script fetches it once and a batch never depends on a download.

tasks.title: Write the PaddleOCR-VL table stage and register it in code
acceptance: `corpus/parsers/paddleocr_vl_table.py` defines the options class (kind `ema_paddleocr_vl`), the model class on `BaseTableStructureModel`, and `register()`, which calls `get_table_structure_factory(allow_external_plugins=True).register(...)`
The model is `PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6` at revision `c5630abae1d940eafe0697512a0325494b02ab42`, bf16 on CUDA, greedy, `max_new_tokens=8192`, `use_cache=True`
`make test-parse` passes `tests/test_docling_parse_env.py::test_table_stage_reads_a_table` (marked `parse` and `gpu`): a synthetic one-page PDF with a 3x3 table gives one table with 9 cells
In .venv the module is not imported by any test of the gate
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Written here; doctool's `src/dw/parsers/paddleocr_vl_stage.py:54-183` is the example (exploration section 3). The model repository's configuration turns the generation cache off, which made one table 7 to 20 times slower in doctool: set `use_cache=True` on every generate call. Registration in code works in Docling 2.153.0 (exploration section 4); no entry point.

tasks.title: Write the docling parser on the Parser protocol
acceptance: `tests/test_parsers_docling_pdf.py::test_missing_extra_in_retrieval_env` passes in the gate: without Docling, `parse()` returns a document whose error starts with `missing_extra`

The converter uses Heron pinned through `LayoutObjectDetectionOptions.from_preset('layout_heron_default')`, RapidOCR with `Rec.lang_type=LangRec.EN`, `Rec.ocr_version=OCRVersion.PPOCRV5`, `Rec.model_type=ModelType.MOBILE`, the table stage of TASK-003, and `allow_external_plugins=True`
A status other than SUCCESS (PARTIAL_SUCCESS included) is returned as an error; `parse()` never raises
`make test-parse` passes `::test_parser_on_fixture_pdf`: `tests/fixtures/fixture_pdf_0.pdf` gives SUCCESS, a page count, and no CJK character
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: `corpus/parsers/base.py:40-58` is the protocol; `llamahub_pdf.py:123` is the example of `missing_extra`. The options and their hash go into run.json. Exploration section 5: `lang=['en']` alone loads the multilingual PP-OCRv6 model, and the first look's 'authorisation 木' comes back.

tasks.title: Post-processing rule 1: join a table that runs over pages
acceptance: `tests/test_docling_post.py::test_split_table_is_joined` passes: a stored document with one table on page 1 and its continuation on page 2 (same column count, adjacent in reading order) becomes one table with two provenance entries, pages 1 and 2
`::test_repeated_header_is_dropped`, `::test_different_columns_are_not_joined` and `::test_join_is_linear` pass; the last joins a 200-part table without rebuilding the element list per part
The rule works on the JSON dict of `doc.raw.json`, with no Docling import, and never changes the input
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: doctool's join is the example (`transforms.py:132-260`): adjacent in reading order, consecutive pages, same label, same `num_cols`, no caption on the continuation, repeated header dropped. Its loop rebuilds all elements for each join (`transforms.py:153-160`); this one walks once. Fixtures are small hand-made JSON files in Docling's format, cut from the exploration's real outputs (`$EMA_RESULTS_DIR/2026-11-26_row17_explore/probe_b/timed/`).

tasks.title: Post-processing rule 2: footnote marks stay marks, footnote texts attach to their table
acceptance: `::test_footnote_mark_is_not_merged_into_number` passes: a cell `12.5\(^{1}\)` becomes the value 12.5 with the mark 1, never 12.51
`::test_footnote_texts_attach_to_table` passes: texts below a table that begin with a mark used in its cells are attached to that table
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Exploration section 4: PaddleOCR-VL writes marks as superscript markup (`FAS\(^{a}\)`), and Docling 2.153.0 exports the footnotes under the repatha table, which 2.132.0 drops.

tasks.title: Post-processing rule 3: turn the table model's markup into text
acceptance: `::test_latex_markup_becomes_text` passes for the cases seen on EMA tables: `\(\pm\)` gives ±, a literal `\n` gives a space, `2.06e^{-14}` gives 2.06e-14, `\(^{a}\)` gives a superscript mark
Each conversion is counted in the counts that run.json and the batch report read
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: doctool's `paddleocr_vl.py:38-153` is the example. Dashes stay as Docling wrote them (proposal: no guess at the original character).

tasks.title: Post-processing rule 4: take title and reference number from the page header
acceptance: `::test_reference_from_page_header` passes: a document whose `EMA/…` reference stands only in a page header gets it at the top of the row's text, where `text_metadata` (first 2,048 characters, `corpus/metadata/text_metadata.py:95`) finds it
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Proposal step 4; the first look found the header layer left out of Docling's export.

tasks.title: Write the writer: three files, a staged move, the failures list, the Markdown text and the Mongo row
acceptance: `::test_failed_write_keeps_previous_folder` passes: a write that fails mid-way leaves the previous folder byte-identical
`::test_failure_is_listed` passes: a failed parse appends `{url, doc_id, error, sha256}` to `<root>/failures.jsonl` and writes no folder

`::test_mongo_row_shape` passes on mongomock: key `(url, 'docling', '<docling version>+<hash8>')`, `content_type` application/pdf, `meta` with doc id, relative folder, source hash and counts, a size guard below 16 MB
Writing the Mongo row is off unless `--write-mongo` is given
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Whether batch 0 writes rows is open (state.json decisions); the default is files only, as the owner's yes says. The Markdown is rendered in the parse environment with docling-core from doc.json; the guard keeps the row under MongoDB's 16 MB (the largest legacy row holds 12.45 million characters).

tasks.title: Write the ranking script: complex-table score and page count per PDF
acceptance: `tests/test_rank_pdfs_by_tables.py` passes: the score of a document is the number of cells in its tables with 8 or more columns, 20 or more rows, or ragged rows; a table needs a separator line
The script writes a ranked JSONL to `config.RESULTS_DIR` with url, score, pages, cache_path, gzip, and documents with pages without text listed after the scored ones
Run read-only on the stores: it reports 58,121 legacy PDF rows and 16,633 with a score above 0 (the exploration's count)
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: The rule is the proposal's (section 'The batches'); exploration section 6 counted 16,633 documents under it, against the review's 5,424 under a stricter rule. Page counts come from the cache (the exploration's count took 567 s with 4 processes).

tasks.title: Write the batch command and wire the parser, the post-processing and the writer into it
acceptance: The command takes a ranked list and a page budget, decompresses a gzip body, skips a document whose folder exists for these options, and replaces its worker process after a set number of documents
A PDF above a set number of pages is parsed in page ranges and joined; a failed or partial document is listed and the batch goes on
It pauses on a schedule (`--pause-every-docs`, `--pause-seconds`) and stops between documents when a stop file exists
`tests/test_parse_pdfs_docling.py` passes in the gate with a stand-in parser: skip of an existing folder, budget, failure listed, stop file honoured
`make test-parse` runs the command on 2 small PDFs end to end
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Proposal section 'The batch command'. The nulojix RMP summary (12.4 million characters) fails on every graph build (row 10's measurement page); the command must list such a document and go on. Runs only in the parse environment.

tasks.title: Write the batch report: rates, failures, sizes, post-processing counts, table numbers, words held
acceptance: The report gives seconds per page for pages without tables, seconds per table and per cell, for the ranked and the random group separately, each with n
It lists every failed or partial document, the bytes per page of each file plain and gzip, and the counts of tables joined, footnotes attached and markup converted

The table-number check: for each table on a page with a text layer, the share of the text layer's numbers inside the table's box that the cells hold, and the share of the cells' numbers that the text layer holds
Words and numbers held against the legacy text of the same document
`tests/test_report_docling_batch.py` passes on two stored fixture documents
`make test` passes and `make lint` passes, each run on its own line
tasks.notes: Proposal section 'What batch 0 reports'. The check cannot see a number in the wrong cell; the page says so.
